answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond, then require validators to slash it when an agent signs conflicting transactions or fails a randomly assigned task. A sybil attacker may create many names cheaply, but must lock real capital behind every one and risks losing it when caught; splitting stake across identities does not multiply influence if voting weight is capped by bonded value. A jetty-side market might price saffron deliveries, while a thread of signed receipts gives validators evidence for disputes.
